description: WS4e: judge accuracy against measured recall@10, at four retrieval depths. Source: data/ws4e/mediator_by_k.csv, rows k in {1,3,5,10}, columns arm, k, recall_at_10, judge_accuracy, judge_accuracy_ci_lo/hi. Same axes as charts/quality-vs-recall.vg.json but on WS4e's 264-question stratum and four SQ8 arms (nprobe 1/4/48/512) instead of WS4's 450 questions and eleven arms; the two are NOT interchangeable. k=3 is drawn so the slide can hold WS4e's depth result against WS6c's, where k=3 beat the shipped limit of 10 on code search; it is monotone between k=1 and k=5 at every arm, and at sq8_np1 its judge accuracy equals k=1's exactly (0.473485), so those two points coincide at the left edge by data, not by error. Judge accuracy from nprobe 1 to nprobe 512 widens with depth (k=1 0.064394, k=3 0.113636, k=5 0.125, k=10 0.143939), the same ordering as data/ws4e/slope_by_k.csv (0.149496, 0.280227, 0.362966, 0.375069). Note this is the np1-to-np512 endpoint range, not max-minus-min: at k=5 the peak arm is np48 (0.651515), so max-min there is 0.159091. Error bars are drawn on k=10 only, the series the slide's guidance rests on. Series colours pass lightness, chroma, CVD separation, normal-vision and contrast checks against the light slide surface, and every series is direct-labelled, so identity is never colour alone. Stage 2's cost band spans np48 (recall 0.958712) to np512 (0.991288): nprobe is the search-cost knob, and 512/48 = 10.7x the IVF cells scanned. The >=4.3x throughput figure is WS2's own measurement (data/ws2/curves_10m.csv, arm ivf_sq8: 8.769665 qps at nprobe 512 against 37.878102 at nprobe 64) and is a bound, not an interpolation, because np48 is cheaper than the measured np64. WS2 and WS4e agree on the index: ivf_sq8 at nprobe 512 reads recall 0.99166 there against 0.991288 here. Every annotation layer carries its own data using the SAME field names as the series data (recall_at_10, judge_accuracy), so all layers share one x and one y definition and the axes resolve once.
